messages:
sam: Heads up — alert from audit pipeline: a service account (service-account-dataflow) kicked off a large export to an external S3 bucket at ~03:12 UTC. ~42GB, ~1.2M rows. Logs show operator role 'analytics_worker' used. :eyes:

priya: Copy. Do we have the export job id? Can we confirm destination bucket is external vs internal?

sam: Job id: export-2026-03-20-0312. Destination: s3://acme-exports-prod (cross-account). Attached log snippet below:

```
{"time":"2026-03-20T03:12:08Z","actor":"service-account-dataflow","role":"analytics_worker","action":"start_export","job_id":"export-2026-03-20-0312","dest":"s3://acme-exports-prod","bytes":44982732800}
```

marcus: That bucket name isn't in our approved outbound buckets list. Noted by DLP rules earlier today. Is the key used a long-lived service account key or short-lived creds?

jenna: Looking at IAM logs: the call used STS AssumeRole via infra-runner-role -> analytics_worker. The STS session is short-lived (1h) but created from a long-lived key on service-account-dataflow.

priya: I'm revoking the long-lived key for service-account-dataflow now and creating a new short-lived credential policy. Will push a lock in 2m. :lock:

infra-bot: revoke-key request acknowledged. Ticket #SEC-2026-112 created.

sam: Thank you. Also can we suspend writes to the target S3 bucket via a block policy (if we have cross-account control) or ask the bucket owner to quarantine?

marcus: We don't control acme-exports-prod. I've opened a contact with their infra lead (diffie@acme.com) and sent an urgent takedown request. Sent DM to @ops-oncall to escalate comms to partner.

ops-oncall: Oncall here — pinged acme infra (cc: security ops). Also initiated an S3 ACL review and requested logs retention copy.

jenna: Forensics note: I pulled a copy of the query that produced the export. It was a largeunnested JOIN across customer_events and sessions with no PII filters. Query below (redacted):

```sql
COPY (
  SELECT ce.*, s.*
  FROM customer_events ce
  JOIN sessions s ON s.session_id = ce.session_id
  WHERE ce.created_at >= '2026-02-01'
) TO 's3://acme-exports-prod/exports/export-2026-03-20-0312' WITH (format csv);
```

sam: That looks like raw customer payload. Treat as possible PII exposure until we confirm otherwise.

priya: OK containment done: revoked long-lived key (service-account-dataflow), invalidated cached STS tokens for that principal, and disabled the analytics_worker role from cross-account assume. Rolling KMS access policy changes next (don't want rotated keys leaked).

marcus: Addendum: audit logs show similar smaller exports from same account on 2026-03-15 and 2026-03-18 to internal buckets. Recommend we run a backfill check for exports >1GB in last 30 days by that principal. I'll run a query.

jenna: For immediate next steps: 1) Confirm whether acme has deleted/quarantined the object 2) Full list of exported tables/columns 3) KMS key grant review (did the service account have Decrypt on our envelope key?)

sam: I've added a short incident timeline in the ticket. Also starting an internal comms thread for Legal/Privacy. CC: @priya for KMS & RBAC notes.

priya: KMS notes: service-account-dataflow had Encrypt/Decrypt via key policy on key-redwood-prod, but only when assumed via analytics_worker. I'm drafting a restrictive key policy and will rotate the data encryption key (DEK) if needed. If we rotate the CMK, we need to coordinate with Dedicated customers.

ops-oncall: Acme confirmed they have quarantined the file and won't download further. They provided a copy of the object checksum. Saving for evidence.

marcus: Running the backfill check now. If I find any other cross-account exports, I'll flag them in the ticket and propose temporary RBAC lock for analytics_worker.

jenna: Post-incident actions I propose: - enforce least-privilege on service-account-dataflow, - require short-lived keys only, - add automated detection for cross-account exports >100MB, - add RBAC rule preventing analytics_worker from cross-account assume by default.

sam: Agreed. Let's have a 30m incident sync in #incidents to triage severity and assign owners. I'll schedule for 10:15 UTC.

priya: I'll draft the KMS policy change and a rollback plan. Also prepping a privacy impact statement for Legal.

infra-bot: Incident meeting created: SEC-2026-112-sync at 10:15 UTC. Calendar invites sent.

sam: Thanks everyone. Keep updates in the ticket; escalate any new exports immediately. :white_check_mark:
